column1: # Does the table's live-set footprint bound the loop?
# v15 killed the instruction-count thesis: 11 fewer instructions per pair, 9-14 ms slower.
# The plan's stated fallback is the other candidate, and it is the one axis no sweep here has
# ever varied. 413 live entries scattered over 16384 slots land on ~408 distinct 128-byte
# lines, so the table holds ~52 KB of L1d resident while a 1 MiB chunk streams through it.
# Twelve of this machine's eighteen cores have 64 KB of L1d. The table-bits sweep could not
# see this: moving the slot count from 2^13 to 2^16 still leaves exactly 413 entries live.
# The only knob that moves the live set is the data, so: 400M rows at 50, 100, 200 and 413
# stations (`OBRC_GEN_STATIONS`, stride-sampled so name lengths stay representative). 50
# stations is ~6 KB of entries and unambiguously resident; 413 is the real workload.
# If the footprint is the bound, ns/row falls as the station count falls, and it falls harder
# at t18 than t8 because t18 is the arrangement that puts work on the narrow cores. If ns/row
# is flat, the table is not the bound, this direction dies here, and what is left is the
# 46 ms read and the 18-21 ms loader.
# Confound to discount: equal rows, unequal bytes. The subsamples differ in mean name length,
# smaller than s413. Read is ~12% of the budget, so that is worth ~0.25% of wall clock —
# a tenth of the smallest effect worth acting on.
# Endpoints are entered twice. Those pairs are the noise floor.
# The files are not kept — 22 GB of them would sit in the page cache that the real dataset
# needs. Half a second each to rebuild:
#   mkdir -p /tmp/obrc-footprint
#       OBRC_GEN_STATIONS=$n ./target/release/generate 400000000 /tmp/obrc-footprint/s$n.txt
#   done
# Result: flat. See the doc comment on src/bin/generate.rs.
s50  t18 (dup)
s413 t18 (dup)
s50  t8
s50  t8 (dup)
s413 t8 (dup)
